chalisa.do1: The lion-like son, the son of Jevar, mighty and steadfast in battle, the son of Queen Bāchal, the hero who wards off calamity: to him I bow.
chalisa.do2: Victory, victory, victory to Gūgā, the incomparable hero of the Chauhān line; having conquered Anaṅgpāl, you became a king among the gods.
chalisa.cau1: Victory, victory, victory to Jāhar, steadfast in battle, destroyer of others' sorrow, the hero of Bāgaṛ. ॥1॥
chalisa.cau2: He is blessed with the boon of Guru Gorakh; Jāharvīr is a peerless warrior. ॥2॥
chalisa.cau3: He is fair of complexion, his face great and broad; a crown is on his head, and his hair is curly. ॥3॥
chalisa.cau4: A bow is on his shoulder, a garland of tulasī beads at his neck, and a sword is slung at his waist for protection. ॥4॥
chalisa.cau5: Gūgā the hero was born, as the world knows, around the year one thousand of the Christian era. ॥5॥
chalisa.cau6: The prince, an ocean of strength and a treasury of virtue, became the support of the sorrowful. ॥6॥
chalisa.cau7: He is the lord of Bāgaṛ, the son of Bāchal and of Jevar; he is a devotee of Hari and a destroyer (of the wicked). ॥7॥
chalisa.cau8: He was called the son of Jevar Rāv, and he raised the name of his mother and father. ॥8॥
chalisa.cau9: All the wishes of whoever prayed to you were fulfilled. ॥9॥
chalisa.cau10: You saved the saints, destroyed the demons and set right the affairs of your devotees. ॥10॥
chalisa.cau11: Wondrous is the tale of Gūgā the hero, to whom Queen Śrīyal was wed. ॥11॥
chalisa.cau12: Queen Bāchal and Rāṇā Jevar were deeply unhappy, being without children. ॥12॥
chalisa.cau13: When a sweeper woman taunted them, life became a burden to them. ॥13॥
chalisa.cau14: The Naulakhā garden lay withered; seeing it again and again, the world's heart ached. ॥14॥
chalisa.cau15: Some days later sādhus came, bringing their disciples, men and women, with them. ॥15॥
chalisa.cau16: Jevar Rāv had a well built; when he wished to open it, ॥16॥
chalisa.cau17: brackish water came out of the well, and the hearts of the king and queen melted in sorrow. ॥17॥
chalisa.cau18: Then the queen sent for an astrologer and asked: For what sin have I not been granted a son? ॥18॥
chalisa.cau19: Tell us some remedy. He said: Win the favour of Guru Gorakh. ॥19॥
chalisa.cau20: If Guru Gorakh is pleased, it is not hard to have a child. ॥20॥
chalisa.cau21: Queen Bāchal sings Gorakh's praises, and does not neglect her observances and dharma. ॥21॥
chalisa.cau22: She practises austerities day and night, and eats a dry flatbread once a day. ॥22॥
chalisa.cau23: She bathes in the months of Kārttika and Māgha, and never forgets the Ekādaśī fast. ॥23॥
chalisa.cau24: She does not miss the full-moon fast, and never turns her face from charity and good works. ॥24॥
chalisa.cau25: Gorakh came with his disciples, and had tents pitched in the Naulakhā garden. ॥25॥
chalisa.cau26: He made the water of the well sweet, and turned the withered garden green. ॥26॥
chalisa.cau27: The sādhus all ate dried fruits and fruits, and sang the praises of their guru. ॥27॥
chalisa.cau28: An Aughaṛ came to beg for alms, and Queen Bāchal told him her sorrows. ॥28॥
chalisa.cau29: The Aughaṛ understood in his mind: By the power of austerity nothing is hard. ॥29॥
chalisa.cau30: He said: Queen, your wish will be fulfilled; it is most needful to take refuge in the Guru. ॥30॥
chalisa.cau31: For twelve years she repeated the Guru's name; then Gorakh knew it in his heart. ॥31॥
chalisa.cau32: He promised to give her a son, and fixed the full-moon day for it. ॥32॥
chalisa.cau33: The deceitful Kāchal did an outrageous thing: she played a cruel trick on the Guru. ॥33॥
chalisa.cau34: Posing as Bāchal, she obtained a son; she felt not the least pity for her sister. ॥34॥
chalisa.cau35: The Aughaṛ told the Guru the secret; then Bāchal received the guggal. ॥35॥
chalisa.cau36: The Guru made it his blessed gift and gave her the guggal grain: Now bear a valiant son. ॥36॥
chalisa.cau37: The mare Līlī and the paṇḍit's wife came to know of it, and Lūnā the maidservant too. ॥37॥
chalisa.cau38: The queen shared out the guggal and ate it, and all who were childless received the remedy. ॥38॥
chalisa.cau39: Narsiṃh the paṇḍit, Līlā the horse, and Bhajjū the kotwāl, steadfast in battle, were born. ॥39॥
chalisa.cau40: Taking fearsome forms, they frighten everyone, and they are dear to Jāharvīr's heart. ॥40॥
chalisa.cau41: When the ninth day of the dark half of Bhādoṃ came, music of rejoicing sounded at Jevar Rāv's house. ॥41॥
chalisa.cau42: The marriage took place, and Gūgā became king; in Saṅgaldīp he was a guest. ॥42॥
chalisa.cau43: He walked the wedding rounds with Queen Śrīyal; Jāhar rules the kingdom of Bāgaṛ. ॥43॥
chalisa.cau44: Kāchal bore Arjan and Sarjan; they remained hostile to Gūgā the hero. ॥44॥
chalisa.cau45: They went to Delhi to make war; the great king Anaṅgpāl marched to the attack. ॥45॥
chalisa.cau46: He besieged all Bāgaṛ; Jāharvīr did not lose heart. ॥46॥
chalisa.cau47: He killed Arjan and Sarjan; Anaṅgpāl laid down his arms. ॥47॥
chalisa.cau48: Clasping his feet, he got himself free; a lion's abode, a shrine, was built. ॥48॥
chalisa.cau49: In that very shrine Gūgā the hero was absorbed; he kindled the ascetic's fire on Gorakh Ṭīlā. ॥49॥
chalisa.cau50: Virtuous servants came there, and served with body, mind and wealth. ॥50॥
chalisa.cau51: The wishes of those who remember Gūgā the hero are fulfilled. ॥51॥
chalisa.cau52: Whoever reads the Jāhar Chālīsā for forty days has all his troubles taken away by the Lord of the world. ॥52॥
chalisa.cau53: May the Creator give them milk and sons; may Guru Gorakhnāth show grace. ॥53॥
